sources.title: Grammatica napoletana
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability_notes: Detailed paradigms (articles, neuter, possessives, verbs incl. essere/avé/tené, avé 'a, metaphony, crasis ô/â/ê). sources.title: Neapolitan language
sources.author: Wikipedia contributors
sources.reliability_notes: Good summary of articles, neuter 'o + doubling ('o nnapulitano vs 'o napulitano), list of doubling triggers, accent/circumflex conventions, avé as sole active auxiliary. Bibliography cites Iandolo 2001 and De Blasi & Imperatore 2001.
sources.relevant_sections: Alphabet and pronunciation; Grammar (articles, verbal conjugation, doubled initial consonants)

sources.title: Proverbi napoletani
sources.author: Wikiquote contributors
sources.reliability_notes: Large collection, many items cite printed sources (e.g. 'I Proverbi di Napoli'). Spelling is not uniform and a few items are from other Campanian varieties (u/i articles): only items in city-Neapolitan form were adopted. Meanings rewritten in our own words.

sources.title: Modi di dire napoletani
sources.author: Wikiquote contributors
sources.reliability_notes: Idioms with explanations and references to printed works (Apicella 'Il frasario napoletano', 'Manuale di napoletanità', contemporary novels). Key: 'Me staje abbuffanno 'a guallera' (annoy to death) and hyperbolic variants ''a guallara a pezzaiuola', 'sfaccimma', 'cazzimma', 'chiaveca'. Meanings rewritten.

sources.title: Wiktionary Neapolitan and Italian entries (machine-readable extract by kaikki.org)
sources.author: Wiktionary contributors; extraction by Tatu Ylonen (wiktextract)
sources.reliability_notes: Neapolitan coverage is thin and mixes regional forms; used only for corroboration: cazzimma (borrowed into Italian from Neapolitan, from cazzo + -imma; cynical opportunism / gratuitous malice), ricchione (vulgar derogatory slur), guaglione, ajere, dimane, accussì, chiagnere.

sources.title: Appuniscë a parlesia? Uno studio sui posteggiatori napoletani e il loro gergo (tesi di laurea magistrale)
sources.author: Anna Fortunato
sources.license: All rights reserved (thesis repository, open access)
sources.reliability_notes: Chapter 2.2 summarizes Radtke (I dialetti della Campania, 1997), Loporcaro (2009) and Cortelazzo et al. (I dialetti italiani, 2002): Southern metaphony, masculine/neuter distinction, doubling after neuter and feminine-plural articles and plural/neuter clitics, partitive n'amico d''o mio, -iello/-ella and -imma suffixes, enclitic possessives (mammeta), tené = possess / stà = locative be, prepositional accusative, jamme ja, ca as polyvalent complementizer, hypothetical clauses with subjunctive in both clauses.

sources.title: Italian Wikipedia articles: Facite ammuina; Scugnizzo; Guappo; Inciucio; Fica (section on regional names: pucchiacca)

sources.title: La frutta realistica ci ha fatto la uallera, video virale
sources.reliability_notes: Contemporary press attestation of the spelling 'uallera' and of the phrase 'ci ha fatto la uallera' glossed as 'ci ha stufato oltre ogni immaginazione'.

sources.title: Slengo: bucchino and related entries (bucchino, bucchin e mammt, bucchinaro, figlie e bucchin, ce fatt 'nu bucchin, kella bucchin e mammt)
sources.linguistic_area: Campania (tagged Reg. Campania; one 'bkkin' entry tagged Puglia, not used)
sources.reliability_notes: Anonymous user entries; region percentages are unexplained. Read directly: /define/bucchino, /define/bucchinaro, /define/figlie-e-bucchin, /define/bucchin-e-mammt, /define/kella-bucchin-e-mammt, /define/ce-fatt-%E2%80%98nu-bucchin. Gives literal sense (fellatio) plus figurative uses: crude dismissal ('va' a fa' quatt bucchin', 'andare a fare i bucchini'), boast/provocation ('famm nu bucchin'), annoyance ('ce fatt 'nu bucchin' = hai rotto), cunning-admiration ('figlie e bucchin', 'bucchinaro'), maternal insult. Facts and short forms only.

sources.title: Slengo: Campania slang entries (Tie, jamm checazz, mamm ro carmn, salutame a' soreta, mocc a mamm't, scassambrella, chiagni e fotti, né pe' bevere né pe' sciacqua', pesce pigliato ca' botta)
sources.reliability_notes: Anonymous user entries tagged Reg. Campania, read via the region index https://slengo.it/browse/region/campania and each /define/<slug> page. Single-contributor entries are treated as unverified; spelling is texting-style and was normalised only minimally to the profile convention.

sources.title: Glosbe: bocchino in Neapolitan
sources.reliability_notes: Lists Neapolitan 'bucchino' (en.wiktionary) and the phrase pair 'fammi un bocchino' / 'famm nu bucchin'. Aggregator of unclear independence from Slengo.

sources.title: Wiktionary: bucchino (Neapolitan)
sources.reliability_notes: Neapolitan noun, plural bucchine, two senses: a mouthful (e.g. of smoke) and, vulgar, fellatio. Gives no region and no etymology.

sources.title: Volgarmente: bucchino
sources.reliability_notes: Anonymous entry tagged Napoli: synonym of oral sex, sometimes also used as insult; no examples.

sources.title: Threads post by @puokemed on Neapolitans opening comments with 'Figlio 'e Bukkì' (17 Dec 2023)
sources.reliability_notes: Social post (replies not readable): observes that many Neapolitans open comments, especially voice messages, with 'Figlio 'e Bukkì'. Used only as evidence of intercalare use; not proof of meaning.

sources.title: Forza Napoli Shop: product 'BANDIERA CIATA FA' SOLO NU BUCCHIN''
sources.reliability_notes: Only the product title is readable (flag 'Ciata fa' solo nu bucchin'', EUR 9.99); no description. The first word 'ciata' could not be decoded, so the phrase is not integrated.

sources.title: Instagram post by ragnar.gk, caption 'Ciata eà sul nu BUCCHIN!' (23 May 2025)
sources.reliability_notes: Fetched page exposes only the caption (tagged #napoli #football) and mocking comments; no definition. Isolated social post, not proof; used only to show the 'Ciata ... sul/solo nu bucchin' formula circulates among Napoli fans.
